messages:
marisol: Team — we received a customer security questionnaire. They want short, factual answers on: logging/PII redaction, encryption (in-transit & at-rest), and current subprocessors + SOC2 status. Need a verified response within ~48h. Who can own checks and provide exact wording?

adrian: Quick infra summary: app middleware performs field-level redaction before logs are sent to the pipeline. Log-processor strips request bodies for public gateway traffic and only retains path, headers (safe set), latency, and status unless flagged for audit. Redis is used as ephemeral cache only (no persistence). TLS 1.2+ enforced in all endpoints; at rest we use AWS KMS CMKs (customer and provider keys supported) with envelope encryption for large artifacts and S3/EBS encryption. Secrets rotated via Vault; access logged.

sam: Can someone paste a tiny example of the scrub logic or point to a short doc I can reference in the customer response? Prefer a 1-2 line snippet we can include.

adrian: Short snippet from platform/logging/scrub.py (sanitized example):
```
REDACT_KEYS = ["email", "ssn", "card_number"]
def redact(payload):
    for k in REDACT_KEYS:
        if k in payload:
            payload[k] = "[REDACTED]"
    return payload
```
Also note: gateway config drops bodies for 3rd-party/public routes; internal audit routes keep bodies under strict retention and ACLs.

dena: Important: do NOT post SOC2 or the full report in this public channel. I will pull the SOC2 summary and the canonical subprocessors CSV from the compliance vault and provide a secure share link to the requester.

sec-bot: Automated: created ticket INF-2210 to validate log retention, scrub rules, and S3 bucket ACLs (assignee needed).

liz: I can take Hosted API verification (INF-2210). Will audit the log-processor config, confirm index retention policies and that request bodies are not stored for public traffic. @marisol please assign INF-2210 to me.

marisol: Assigning INF-2210 to @liz. Please include exact bucket names and retention windows in the ticket so I can reference them in the reply.

adrian: Confirming Redis in prod clusters is configured with persistence off (both RDB and AOF disabled). Snapshots are not taken for caches; any backups are encrypted and access-controlled via IAM roles. KMS alias in prod: alias/redwood-prod-kms (will paste ARN into INF-2210).

dena: Subprocessors (canonical CSV in vault) — quick list for the questionnaire: AWS (infrastructure), Cloudflare (CDN/edge), Datadog (metrics/alerts), Sentry (error tracking), Okta (SSO), Stripe (billing), PostHog (product analytics). I'll get the latest CSV and SOC2 summary from /vault/compliance and share via secure link per policy.

sam: For the encryption blurb I'll draft: "Data in transit is encrypted using TLS; data at rest is encrypted using AWS KMS-managed CMKs with envelope encryption for large artifacts. Secrets are rotated and access is audited via Vault and IAM." Is that OK to include?

adrian: Yes, that wording is accurate. Add that we support customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private customers where required.

marisol: To-do so we can finalize the questionnaire:
- dena: deliver SOC2 summary + current subprocessors CSV via secure vault link (do not paste reports here)
- liz: complete INF-2210 verification (buckets, retention windows, scrub rules)
- adrian: paste full KMS ARN and confirm Redis config in INF-2210
- sam: draft the customer answers and post here for quick review

liz: I'll update INF-2210 today with bucket names, retention (30 days by default for request metadata indices), and a short screenshot of the log-processor rule that drops bodies.

dena: Links (internal vault): /vault/compliance/soc2/summary-2025.pdf and /vault/compliance/subprocessors/current.csv — will DM the secure share per policy to the customer contact.

marisol: Thanks all. Once INF-2210 is updated and dena shares the secure links, I'll finalize and send the questionnaire. Ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
